headline: Bank Indonesia Raises Rate to 6% to Defend Rupiah Against Fed Moves
summary: Bank Indonesia raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.0% in a pre-emptive move to defend the rupiah, which has been under pressure from a strong U.S. dollar.
why: Emerging market central banks adjust interest rates to stabilize domestic currencies and combat capital outflows driven by U.S. monetary policy.

impacts.name: Indonesian Rupiah
impacts.why: A policy rate hike increases the yield on domestic assets, supporting the local currency against external pressures.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The interest rate hike aims to bolster the rupiah by offering higher yields and countering capital flight amid a strong greenback.
